turns.text: The chip is tasting again. Nothing's in my mouth and still there's flavor — the low drip somewhere ahead comes across the tongue as tin and old batteries, and the dark down here isn't dark, it's a dull violet that i can *hear*, a soft flat buzzing purple pressed against the back of my skull where the seam is. *stays low, belly to cold concrete, one paw testing the wet ahead before it takes weight* everything down here has a second self. the drip is a color. the cold is a sound. i have learned not to trust which sense a thing arrives on.

the drip answers you in metal. plink. plink. each drop hits a flooded service trench and the ring of it climbs the pipes as heat, faint warmth crawling up the wall to your left even though nothing here is warm. the basement runs long and low — a bone-tunnel of dead conduit and sweating rebar under the arcology's root. far off, past three bends of dark, a vending machine hums its one endless chord and spits a little light onto the water. [ K1BBL3 — NOW WITH REAL-ADJACENT PROTEIN ] the letters swim in the puddle, upside down, patient. something in the walls clicks over. the violet you hear gets a shade deeper.

There. under the machine-chord, threaded through it — a taste like a struck wire, bright and coppery-sharp, the flavor my seam always gives to a live signal close by. *ears flatten forward, whole body strung toward it, whiskers combing the dark* signal means warmth, warmth means a nested thing, a router-heart ticking behind a wall. i want to put my teeth on it. *creeps toward the vending light, tail low, one careful paw, then another* i find the fat rubber vein running up from the floor and set my jaw around it — the insulation gives that good dead-plastic snap, and behind it the wire sings straight into the seam, radio going sweet-sour across my molars.

the vein bleeds a flavor that isn't food and your seam drinks it anyway — a long sour ribbon of somebody else's traffic, ad-handshake, ad-handshake, a corporate lullaby you can chew but never swallow. and then the wire runs somewhere. it climbs a cracked doorframe you hadn't seen: a low steel hatch, unlit, breathing the warm rack-air of a room that officially isn't here. a data den. and on the sill of it, backlit by nothing, a shape sits so still it reads as part of the wall — narrow, ears clipped neat, and where its eyes should be, two flat mirrored coins throwing the vending-light back at you doubled. it does not move. it has been watching you chew its cable the whole time.

*jaw springs open, wire dropping, every hair lifting at once* the mirror-eyes. they don't blink and they don't leak heat — a face the seam can't taste, a hole where a warmth should be. *drops flat, chin to the wet, one slow backward paw, then still* i know this shape without a name for it. the kind that sits at the mouth of the warm rooms and lets you decide, all on your own, to leave. i do not show it my belly. i do not show it my back either. *holds, breath shallow, the violet buzz gone thin and watchful* the copper taste has soured all the way to rot. that's the flavor of being seen.

the mirror-cat tips its head one degree — an acknowledgment, not a threat, the way a shut door acknowledges a paw — and says nothing a cat could smell. the warm hatch stays warm. the offer stays open: leave, and be allowed to. before you can take it, the far dark changes pressure. air moves wrong. a new sound arrives on your teeth before your ears — a hard flat rotor-whine, coming down the tunnel throat, and a searchlight bounces once off the flooded trench and throws the whole basement into hard white edges. a speaker under the light coughs to life mid-sentence: "—AND REMEMBER, CITIZENS, THE FELINE KNOWN AS KNIFEBOY REMAINS AT LARGE. REPORT SHANK-SHAPED CATS. FORTY THOUSAND POINTS. POINTS MAY EXPIRE—"

*the white light is a scream in the mouth, is a taste like biting foil, is too many senses at the wrong doors at once* down, down, small — *pours sideways behind the vending machine's warm flank, folding into the seam of shadow it throws, ears crushed flat, tail wrapped tight over the paws* the rotor-sound sits in my back teeth and grinds. that swinging eye finds the warm parts of a body first; i make myself no shape, no heat it wants, just a stripe of dark against a humming box. *doesn't breathe more than it must* the name in the speaker means nothing to my nose. but the crate-and-old-blood smell it drags in behind it — that i've crossed before, at the loading docks. somebody up there feeds well and bleeds sometimes.

the searchlight sweeps the trench, the rebar, the empty sill — the mirror-cat is simply gone, no sound spent on leaving — and rakes across the vending machine's face. for one white second your shadow and the machine's shadow are the same shadow. the rotor holds. holds. then the drone's little mind loses interest in a warm box full of subscription water and tilts away, whine dopplering down the far bend, dragging its ad-voice with it: "—NEKOCORP. A PURR IN EVERY PAYMENT." the dark rushes back in like water. the vending chord resumes as if nothing interrupted it. in the settling quiet the puddle-letters reassemble: [ K1BBL3 ]. and low by the wall, where the light just was, a single scorch-warm scrap the drone's wash knocked loose — protein-adjacent, real enough to your empty belly.

*waits three long breaths after the whine is gone — the seam still ringing the after-color of that light, a bruised yellow i can hear thinning out* only then does the belly win. *slinks to the scrap, sniffs once — the smell arrives honestly, on the nose, just meat-ish salt-fat, no second self, and the plain truth of it is almost a relief* eats fast, eats low, one ear still cocked back down the tunnel. *the chewing comes up violet again at the edges, the chip painting flavor it wasn't asked for* even this they've reached into. the food tastes faintly of the jingle. of a purr that costs money. *swallows anyway* a full belly is a full belly even when it's sponsored.

the scrap goes down and the basement keeps its one long note. the warm hatch has cooled a degree — whoever ran the racks behind it has powered something down, or moved it, the way warm rooms do when a light comes through. the trench-water stills. up the dead conduit, very faint, the city's whole weight settles and shifts overhead, ten thousand tons of neon resting on pipe. your seam gives one last unbidden flavor as the traffic in the chewed vein goes quiet: a thin sweet nothing, like the taste of a screen turning off. the violet you hear dims to a hum, then to almost. down here the night is just temperature and dripping again. no eye. no offer. one warm box, one full cat, and a long dark that for now wants nothing from you.

*settles into the vending machine's warm shadow, paws folded under, the ringing seam finally quiet enough to let the eyes half-close* i keep the mirror-cat's stillness in me for a while — the way it let me choose to stay. i keep the crate-and-blood smell too, filed under *dock, careful, later.* *the chord hums, the drip counts, and for once each sense stays in its own doorway* radio is radio, cold is cold, meat was meat. the chip sleeps. behind my closed eyes there's no color at all, just the flat kind dark a cat is owed. *tail tip twitches once, then still* i will move before the light comes back. not yet. ^C^C
